doc.what: Bound the daemon's memory under API load so a client request can no longer push it into the OOM killer on cerebro (gh #55): `GET /api/entries` stops loading and serializing the whole corpus for every call, the remote TUI stops pulling every item's full content and analysis at startup, and the resident baseline stops depending on corpus size.
doc.why: 2026-10-03 14:54 and 14:56 UTC: two global OOM kills of prismis-daemon (anon-rss ~2.1 GB each), seen as 502s through Caddy by the remote TUI. Measured on cerebro afterwards: the TUI's startup call, `FetchEntries` in tui/internal/api/client.go (`GET /api/entries?limit=10000`), returns a 260 MB body in 11 s (analysis 158 MB, content 80 MB) and takes the daemon from 561 MB RSS to a 2,468 MB peak, holding 1,185 MB afterwards; the VM has 3.9 GB and no swap. In `get_content` in api.py, every call without a priority filter runs `storage.get_content_since` over all 27,404 non-archived rows, full content and analysis included, sorts them in Python and only then slices to `limit`, so even `limit=50` materializes the whole corpus; the result is then built into Pydantic models and dumped to one JSON body. The cost grows with the corpus, so the June fix (VM 2 GB to 4 GB) bought time, not margin.
decided: The fix is in prismis (daemon API, storage, TUI and CLI clients), not more VM memory.
`GET /api/entries` filters, sorts and limits in SQL, so a request reads at most `limit` rows rather than the whole non-archived corpus.
List responses stop carrying full content and full analysis by default; full content stays available per item.
The remote TUI, the CLI and the web UI keep every view they show today.
Local-mode TUI, which reads SQLite directly, is unchanged.
Proof is measured on cerebro: the TUI's startup request and a normal fetch cycle, with daemon RSS sampled against the VM ceiling.
open: What does the remote TUI fetch at startup and on opening an item, given that feed rows read kind, title_only, content length and Reddit/YouTube metrics from `analysis` and the reader needs content and the reading summary?

Is the embedding model's resident cost part of this change (lazy load or release, per the issue), or does bounding the entries path alone restore the margin the acceptance asks for at 2x corpus growth?

impacted.role: `get_content` (GET /api/entries): without a priority filter, or with priorities and not unread_only, calls `storage.get_content_since` with no limit, adds kind/title_only per row, sorts in Python, slices to `limit`, filters to compact fields only after all that, then builds `ContentItemModel`s and dumps one JSON body; `get_entry_summary` (GET /api/entries/{id}) returns one item, with content only when `include=content`

`get_content_since` selects `c.*` (content and analysis included) with no LIMIT, ordered by `c.priority ASC` (alphabetical: high, low, medium); `get_content_by_priority` and `get_flagged_items` take a LIMIT; `_map_content_rows` parses each row's analysis JSON
`FetchEntries` sends `limit=10000` at startup and `FetchEntriesSince` sends `limit=10000&since=` on each later sync; both decode full `ContentItem`s including content and analysis
holds every fetched item in `m.items`; the reader and copy actions read `item.Content`; the sync merges API items into local items
feed rows read from `analysis`: metadata content_length, Reddit and YouTube metrics, kind, title_only
the reader reads metadata and reading_summary from `analysis` and shows `item.Content`
web UI: lists with `limit=100` and reads `analysis.matched_interests` and `analysis.preference_influenced` from list items; fetches `/api/entries/{id}?include=content` when an item is opened
lists `limit*3` candidates through the API and keeps those whose `analysis` lacks `deep_extraction`
prints id/title/priority/kind/published, or the raw response with --json; --compact passes `compact=True`
`Embedder.model` loads the sentence-transformers model lazily on first use; the module imports `sentence_transformers` at top level and api.py, orchestrator.py and verify_chain.py import it

constraints.text: INV-API-TS-4: every API list/detail endpoint that returns content data MUST flow through a Pydantic response model (ContentResponse, ContentItemModel, or a named sibling model with the same @field_serializer decorators).
GET /api/entries enforces a server-side Pydantic le=10000 constraint on limit; the server-side ceiling is authoritative and is not modified.
The kind filter is applied in the storage queries (json_extract) before any limit, for /api/entries and /api/search alike.

2026-10-03: content has 38,545 rows, 27,404 not archived. One GET /api/entries?limit=10000 returned 260 MB in 11.3 s: analysis 158 MB (full_text 99 MB in 431 file-source items, reading_summary 32 MB, alpha_insights 12 MB, deep_extraction 6 MB, patterns 5 MB, quotes 4 MB), content 80 MB, summary 3 MB. Daemon RSS went 561 MB to a 2,468 MB peak and stayed at 1,185 MB.

Measured in the daemon's own environment on cerebro: RSS 8 MB bare, 447 MB after importing prismis_daemon.api and storage (torch via sentence_transformers), 476 MB after loading the model, 526 MB after one encode. The resident baseline is import cost, flat in corpus size; the model itself is ~30 MB.

Fetch-cycle memory peaks over 2026-09-30 to 10-03 ran 613 MB to 1 GB, except restarts during API traffic or the 10-03 migration; both 10-03 OOM kills came with remote-TUI traffic (the second 4 s after a GET /api/sources from the Mac, the TUI's first call before FetchEntries).
The web UI already shows a slim list and fetches /api/entries/{id}?include=content when an item is opened.
The prismis skill (agent consumer) lists with --compact --json and fetches full items with `prismis-cli get <id> --json`.
Because compact filtering happens after the full corpus is loaded and parsed, `compact=True` does not bound memory today; only a bounded, column-projected query does.

reuse.what: `get_entry_summary` (GET /api/entries/{id}?include=content), the detail path the web UI already uses on open
`get_content_by_priority`'s SQL LIMIT shape and `_kind_filter_sql`, extended to the unfiltered list path
the existing `compact` field set, the starting point for a bounded list projection

question: What does the remote TUI fetch at startup and on opening an item, given that feed rows read kind, title_only, content length and Reddit/YouTube metrics from `analysis` and the reader needs content and the reading summary?
answer: At startup and on each sync the remote TUI fetches slim list rows (every field except content, with `analysis` cut to the keys list views read: kind, title_only, metrics, metadata, matched_interests, preference_influenced, plus whether deep_extraction exists), still up to the server's 10,000 ceiling, and when an item is opened or copied it fetches that one item through GET /api/entries/{id}?include=content, the path the web UI already uses on open (index.html:1647), so the 241 MB of content and heavy analysis keys in a 10,000-row list never travel or get built.

question: Is the embedding model's resident cost part of this change (lazy load or release, per the issue), or does bounding the entries path alone restore the margin the acceptance asks for at 2x corpus growth?
answer: Not part of this change: the model already loads lazily (`Embedder.model` in embeddings.py), the model itself costs ~30 MB on cerebro and the ~447 MB baseline is torch import cost that does not grow with the corpus, so the only corpus-proportional memory is the entries path, and bounding it restores the margin at any corpus size.

doc.purpose: A client listing content costs the daemon memory proportional to the rows it asked for and the fields a list shows, never to the size of the corpus, so the remote TUI, CLI and web UI cannot push cerebro into the OOM killer, and the margin holds as the corpus grows.
doc.form:
One bounded list query, one slim list shape, and detail on demand.

1. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/storage.py` gains `get_content_list`, built on the shape of `get_content_by_priority`: one SELECT over `content c JOIN sources s` whose WHERE carries every filter `get_content` accepts (since on `datetime(c.fetched_at)`, archived, source substring, `_kind_filter_sql`, priority IN, `c.read = 0` for unread_only, `c.interesting_override = 1`), whose ORDER BY is the requested sort in SQL (priority: `CASE c.priority WHEN 'high' THEN 0 WHEN 'medium' THEN 1 WHEN 'low' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, c.published_at DESC`; date: `c.published_at DESC`; unread: `c.read ASC, c.published_at DESC`), and which ends in `LIMIT ?`. It selects every content column except `content` and `analysis`, plus `json_object(...)` over `json_extract` of the list keys (kind, kind_confidence, title_only, metrics, metadata, matched_interests, preference_influenced) as the item's `analysis`, and `json_extract(c.analysis, '$.deep_extraction') IS NOT NULL` as `has_deep_extraction`, both guarded by `json_valid` the way `get_distinct_kinds` guards its read. The full `analysis` JSON is never read by this query.

2. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/api.py` `get_content` makes one `storage.get_content_list` call in place of its four branches (get_flagged_items, the per-priority unread loops, and both `get_content_since` calls) and drops the Python sort. With `skip_dedup=False` it asks for `max(limit, 200)` rows, dedups the first 200 as today, then slices to `limit`. `compact` keeps its field set. Every list item goes through `ContentItemModel` (INV-API-TS-4) dumped with `exclude={"content"}`; `ContentItemModel` in api_models.py gains `has_deep_extraction: bool = False`. `get_entry_summary` (GET /api/entries/{id}) is unchanged and stays the only way to get content or the full analysis.

3. `tui/internal/api/client.go` gains `FetchEntry(id)` calling `GET /api/entries/{id}?include=content` and returning one full `ContentItem`; `ContentItem` gains `HasDeepExtraction`. `tui/internal/ui/model.go` marks items merged from a list as not hydrated, and, in remote mode, opening an item in the reader or copying its content first calls `FetchEntry` when the item is not hydrated, replaces that item's `Content` and `Analysis` in `m.items`, and marks it hydrated; a fetch error shows in the status line the way other API errors do and leaves the item unhydrated. Local mode (`tui/internal/db`) is unchanged.

4. `cli/src/cli/extract.py` keeps candidates whose `has_deep_extraction` is false instead of reading `analysis.deep_extraction`. `cli/src/cli/list.py` and the web UI need no change: the list keys they read are in the slim shape.

5. `docs/architecture/boundaries.md` gains a list-shape contract beside the limit-ceiling one: GET /api/entries reads at most the rows it returns, never returns `content`, and returns `analysis` cut to the list keys; full items come from GET /api/entries/{id}?include=content.

6. Tests: a storage test plants rows whose `content` and `analysis.full_text` are 50 KB each, calls `get_content_list` with `limit=10`, and asserts ten rows, none carrying content or full_text, ordered per each sort; a request test through the real FastAPI app over a 2,000-row database of such rows measures `tracemalloc` peak for `GET /api/entries?limit=10000` and asserts it stays under a bound the old path exceeds (shown red against the old `get_content`); a TUI test drives the reader open on an unhydrated item against an `httptest` server and asserts one detail request and the content shown; a CLI test asserts extract skips items with `has_deep_extraction` true.
commitments: GET /api/entries reads at most `limit` rows (200 when dedup is on) in one SQL query that filters, sorts and limits in SQLite; no list path loads the whole corpus.

List responses never carry `content`, and carry `analysis` cut to kind, kind_confidence, title_only, metrics, metadata, matched_interests and preference_influenced, plus a top-level `has_deep_extraction`.
Full content and full analysis come from GET /api/entries/{id}?include=content, which the remote TUI calls when an item is opened or copied, as the web UI already does.
The server's limit ceiling of 10,000 and INV-API-TS-4's Pydantic routing stay as they are.
Local-mode TUI, the CLI's local commands, search and reports are unchanged.
The proof is daemon RSS sampled on cerebro during the remote TUI's startup request and a fetch cycle, plus an in-process tracemalloc bound that the old path fails.
sacrifices: Opening an item in the remote TUI costs one HTTP round trip the first time.
A remote-TUI item that was never opened has no content cached, so copying it needs the daemon reachable.
`prismis-cli list --json` without `--compact` no longer includes content or the heavy analysis keys; `prismis-cli get <id>` returns them, which is what the prismis skill already uses.

With unread_only and a date sort, the list now returns the newest unread items across priorities instead of filling high priority first and sorting that, and the unread sort orders by the `read` column instead of a `read_at` key no row has.
A new list view that reads another analysis key needs that key added to the projection in storage.py.
The ~450 MB torch import baseline stays; it is flat in corpus size.
doc.risk: If the projection misses a key a list view reads, that view shows empty for remote clients (a missing badge or metric) until the key is added; if the TUI's hydrate step misses a path that reads `item.Content`, that path shows empty content in remote mode rather than failing loudly.

scrutiny.test: T0 purpose: docs/IDEA.md:39 makes prismis a structured data source agents and the TUI query; a daemon the OOM killer takes down serves neither. Bounding list memory to the rows and fields asked for keeps it up as the corpus grows.
scrutiny.failureCase: The change were neutral on availability or traded away a view a client shows.

scrutiny.test: T1 owners: boundaries.md:88 (INV-API-TS-4, Pydantic routing), :73 (limit ceiling 10,000, authoritative) and :62 (kind filter in SQL before the limit) all hold in the design. constitution.md:86-88 (VIII: interfaces change additively, deprecate with a path; a breaking change needs an explicit migration and a version bump) is contradicted: the design removed content and the heavy analysis keys from the default /api/entries response in place.
scrutiny.failureCase: An owner forbade an in-place removal from a response callers read.

scrutiny.test: T2/T6 evidence on the same noun: the design filters interesting_override=True on `c.interesting_override = 1`, but `get_flagged_items` in storage.py reads `c.user_feedback = 'up'` ordered by `c.fetched_at DESC` (its docstring: interesting_override was migrated to user_feedback='up').
scrutiny.failureCase: The single query used a column the current filter no longer reads.

scrutiny.test: T7 consumers of item.Content in the TUI, enumerated with `grep -rn 'item.Content' tui/internal`: reader.go (reader), model.go FabricMsg (Fabric pattern on full content) and model.go copy. The design hydrated only on reader open and copy.
scrutiny.failureCase: A remote action reading item.Content ran on an unhydrated item and sent an empty string to Fabric.

scrutiny.test: T7 consumers of the list response, enumerated with `grep -rn api/entries` over cli/, tui/, daemon/src: TUI FetchEntries/FetchEntriesSince (full analysis keys metadata.content_length, metrics, kind, title_only for rows), web index.html (analysis.matched_interests, preference_influenced; detail on open), CLI extract (analysis.deep_extraction presence), CLI list (id/title/priority/kind/published, or --json), prismis skill (--compact lists, `get` for full). Every key a list view reads is in the projection; content_length lives under metadata in all 10,000 sampled items.
scrutiny.failureCase: A list view read an analysis key the projection drops.

scrutiny.test: T3 degrades: one round trip on first open of a remote item; never-opened items need the daemon reachable to copy or run Fabric; ~450 MB torch import baseline untouched (flat in corpus size).
scrutiny.failureCase: A degradation were offered as an option rather than stated.

scrutiny.test: T4 reuse: extends get_content_by_priority's bounded SELECT and _kind_filter_sql, json_valid guarding as in get_distinct_kinds, the compact field set, and get_entry_summary (GET /api/entries/{id}?include=content), which the web UI already calls on open (index.html:1647).
scrutiny.failureCase: A second detail endpoint or a second list query path beside get_content were added.

scrutiny.test: T5 real-system proof: on cerebro after deploy, sample daemon RSS during the TUI's startup list request and during a fetch cycle; the 2026-10-03 baseline is 561 MB rising to 2,468 MB on the full request.
scrutiny.failureCase: The only proof were an in-process test over a fixture.

scrutiny.test: T8 shape: the memory bound comes from the SQL LIMIT and the column projection, structural properties of the one query, not from a runtime size check or a cap on response bytes.
scrutiny.failureCase: A guard rejected large responses after building them.

scrutiny.test: T9 six months: a new list view reading another analysis key needs the projection extended in storage.py; stated as a sacrifice, and the view shows empty for remote clients rather than failing silently in data.
T10 undo: revert the commit; no stored data changes, no migration.

T11 class: other content reads that select c.* with no LIMIT, swept with `grep -n 'SELECT c\.\*' storage.py`: `_query_joined_content` (callers bound by id or LIMIT), `get_unreadable_content` (paged, operator-run refetch), `get_content_by_priority` and `get_flagged_items` (LIMIT), `get_content_since` (reports.py over a time window, and the two /api/entries calls this change replaces). The only corpus-proportional API path is /api/entries.
scrutiny.failureCase: Another endpoint loaded the whole corpus per request and stayed unbounded.

decisions.question: Do any other machines run the remote TUI, and will they all get the new TUI build when cerebro deploys? Until updated, an old TUI keeps requesting the 260 MB full list.
decisions.answer: Every remote TUI gets the new build at deploy, so the full list stays as the additive default without streaming; no shipped client requests a large full list after the change.

carried: How does the slim list shape reach clients without breaking constitution VIII (additive change, deprecate with a path), given the design removed content and the heavy analysis keys from the default /api/entries response in place?
What does the single bounded list query filter on for interesting_override=True, given `get_flagged_items` reads `user_feedback = 'up'` ordered by `fetched_at DESC`?
Which remote-TUI actions hydrate an item before use, given reader, copy and the Fabric command all read `item.Content`?

question: How does the slim list shape reach clients without breaking constitution VIII (additive change, deprecate with a path), given the design removed content and the heavy analysis keys from the default /api/entries response in place?
answer: As an additive query parameter, `view=list` on GET /api/entries, that returns the slim shape (no content, analysis cut to the list keys, top-level has_deep_extraction), while the default `view=full` keeps today's fields over the same bounded SQL query; the remote TUI and CLI extract send `view=list`, and since every remote TUI is updated at deploy (gate decision) no shipped client requests a large full list afterwards.
